claims.text: The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a coarse BCC phase structure.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has limited tensile ductility.
Nb and V can be incorporated into HfZrTiTa0.53 at approximately 0.2 atomic fraction each through repeated suspension melting.
Adding Nb and V will stabilize the BCC phase of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Adding Nb and V will refine the BCC microstructure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Nb and V additions alter the alloy's electronic and atomic-size parameters.
The altered electronic and atomic-size parameters produce a more uniform and stabilized BCC phase.
A more uniform and stabilized BCC phase reduces stress concentrations.
Reduced stress concentrations facilitate plastic deformation under tensile loading.
The Nb- and V-modified alloy will exhibit at least 50% greater tensile uniform elongation than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will maintain yield strength above 786 MPa.
The modified alloy will maintain compressive strength above 1314 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain impact-triggered energy-release performance similar to that of baseline HfZrTiTa0.53.
Prior studies established impact-triggered energy-release performance for baseline HfZrTiTa0.53.
The predicted ductility improvement applies at room temperature under quasi-static tensile loading near 10^-3 s^-1.
Behavior at elevated temperatures or other strain rates may differ from the room-temperature quasi-static prediction.

contradictions.description: These fields treat impact-triggered energy release as established for baseline HfZrTiTa0.53, whereas no cited evidence record supports impact-energy performance for that alloy system.

The tests are described as being under similar or quasi-static conditions, but an impact-triggered energy-release test necessarily involves a distinct dynamic loading regime; the impact strain rate and matching criterion are not specified.
